lesson.subtitle: Lesson 13 -- What Should I Do?
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Renato | Lesson 13 -- What Should I Do?

listenings.text: Morning, everybody. A few words for the new members before you go down to the water. First thing. You should show up ten minutes early. We start at six thirty, not at six forty. If you are late, you paddle out on your own and nobody is watching you. Second thing. In the water you should sit wide for the first week and just watch. Wait your turn. The wave will come. And you should not paddle for every set you see, because the older members are watching and they remember. Last thing, and this is the important one. If you make a mistake out there, and everybody does, apologize. Say sorry and keep going. Nobody here has a problem with a beginner. We have a problem with people who do not say sorry.

Hey, it is Tess. I forgot two things this morning, so listen to this before you get on the plane. School first. On your first day you should not sit alone at lunch. I know it feels awkward, but ask somebody what they are listening to and that is it, you are in. Second thing, and my brother says this is the most important one. When people here ask how you are, they are not really asking. You should say good thanks, how are you, and keep walking. If you stop and tell them everything about your week, they think you are strange. And one more. You should call my mum when you land in Perth. She wants to know that you arrived. See you in February.

items.situation: A new member shows up ten minutes late for the first session. Give him two pieces of advice.

Somebody drops in on you at your home break and says nothing. What should he do?

A tourist wants to surf your beach tomorrow. Two things to do, one thing not to do.
